title: LADA Beerteam vs Cluster Pucks, Nov 14
notes: Renton, the re-aimed camera (renton2nov) already rolled about 0.9 degrees on Nov 14, a day earlier than the Nov 15 games it was first seen on; run as renton2nov. Beerteam away in light blue on the left bench. Periods from the board's clock (1-1084, 1173-2254, 2350-3731); the video starts at the opening faceoff. The video was downloaded with the user's browser cookies after YouTube's bot check.

Played: 11 skaters and Mayorov #1 in goal, the 12 the game sheet marks. Petrov #18 is new to roster.json, entered as a sub without a LADA id (TK's roster has a Petrov #18 with id 12165, Y's with 20416). Absent: #7, #10, #11, #12, #13, #16, #20, #25, #41, #56, #61, #70, #76, #87, #94. Cluster Pucks' #12 BERRY, #54 PIZANO and #88 MAKAIO (white with navy and yellow trim) pass our light-blue crop test; the 170 reads of "12" were BERRY's, so Kondratenko #12 is absent.

#54 is Pfeifer (the sheet's name, PFEIFER 54 read on his back; roster.json's #54 is the sub Semenov), the goalie who subbed for Doofers on Sep 27 and Blue Wings on Nov 15, here a skater in a dark green jersey with red and white stripes. The jersey test drops him: no tracks, no crops, no review rows. His 15 shifts (33:46) were traced by eye by seven subagents, every edge a step through the bench door or over the boards, and entered as 15 `on` and 17 `off` spans (green54/ in the work folder has the brief and the answers). The first solve, without him, had spread his minutes over the other ten. He has no positions, so the ice map and zone time have nothing of his.

run2.py changed for this game: a roster player named by an `on` span is solved even without 20 s of labeled track (the solver used to leave such a player out and drop his spans silently), and the solve warns about spans whose player it leaves out. regress.py: 45 same, 2 differ (Blue Wings' Sep 20 and Sep 27, as before the change).

Goal times from the goal checkers; the puck was not seen crossing the line on any of the six (crease scrambles), so each t is the last jam or the goalie's reaction. Goal 2 (theirs): the first two checkers took #76's play from the half-wall at 1254.2 for the scoring shot and put the goal at 1256.0, and the first clip's replay showed #76 and not the scorer, which the user caught. A third checker, told to follow the sheet's scorer, found #36 Trefethen (number and nameplate read) at the far point: #76's puck rolled up to him, he picked it up at 1255.6-1255.8 and carried it to the net, swinging at about 1256.4; t 1256.75 is the middle of the 1256.4-1257.1 in which it went in (low confidence, the puck not seen). The clip follows a hand trace of him (traces/goal-2.csv). Goal 4: two checkers read the passer behind the net as #27 Egiazarov; the sheet's assist is #37 Akulov and stands. Goal 6: the drive to the net is #5 Zhaksilikov's and #44 was not seen in the build-up; the sheet has Kleiman #69 from Tverskoy #44 and stands; the scorer's number was not read.

Penalties: Kleiman #69 and their #51, coincident roughing minors at 10:00 of the 1st, played 5 on 5 (five light blue and five white counted at the faceoff): no kill, #69 off 465.5-699 in the box; the infraction is a board battle beside their net at about 449.5 (low confidence). Papusha #24, interference at 2:21 of the 2nd: a delayed call after a tangle beside our net at 2110.5, kill 2114.5-2254 and 2350-2395 (3:00 on the board; the operator took about 29 s off over the intermission). Their #11's minor in the 3rd is a double minor on the sheet and a single 2:00 on the board.

By hand: the spans for #54 above; clip arguments for goal-6 (no pass: the checker's pass came after its shot) and for goal-1, goal-2, penalty-69 and penalty-24 (hand traces of the player's skates in traces/, since #69 is untracked at the net on goal 1 and tracks 198 and 395 carry other players in the penalty windows; track 395, labeled #24, is #27 from about 2100, both on the ice then). The lineup checkers added 11 spans in one round; the lineup check ended OK at 102% of expected ice time in each period.
